tasks.intro: Here's how to make an HTTP GET request in {lang}.
tasks.notes: Always check the response status code and handle network errors. Set a timeout so a slow endpoint can't hang your program. For JSON APIs, decode the body before parsing.

languages.python:
import urllib.request
import json

def http_get(url: str, timeout: int = 10) -> dict:
    req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={'User-Agent': 'cos/1.0'})
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode())

# Example (JSONPlaceholder):
data = http_get('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1')
print(data['name'])

# With the `requests` library (nicer API):
# import requests
# resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
# resp.raise_for_status()
# data = resp.json()
languages.bash:
# curl
curl -s https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1

# curl + jq to extract a field:
curl -s https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 | jq ".name"

tasks.intro: Here's how to make an HTTP POST request with a JSON body in {lang}.
tasks.notes: Set the `Content-Type: application/json` header when sending a JSON body, and make sure to encode the payload as JSON (not a Python dict or JS object) — forgetting the encoding is the most common 400-error cause.

languages.python:
import urllib.request
import json

def http_post(url: str, payload: dict, timeout: int = 10) -> dict:
    body = json.dumps(payload).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(
        url, data=body,
        headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'User-Agent': 'cos/1.0'},
        method='POST',
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
        return json.loads(resp.read().decode())

# Example:
print(http_post('https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts',
                {'title': 'hi', 'body': 'there', 'userId': 1}))

# With `requests`:
# import requests
# resp = requests.post(url, json=payload, timeout=10)
# resp.raise_for_status()
# print(resp.json())
languages.bash:
# curl POST with a JSON body:
curl -s -X POST https://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/posts \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d "{\"title\": \"hi\", \"body\": \"there\", \"userId\": 1}"

tasks.intro: Here's a {lang} script that checks whether a website or URL is up.
tasks.notes: Treat any 2xx–3xx status as 'up' — 4xx/5xx or a network error means 'down'. Always set a timeout so a hung endpoint can't block your script. A HEAD request is cheaper than GET for this job when the server supports it.

languages.python:
import urllib.request
import urllib.error


def is_up(url: str, timeout: int = 10) -> bool:
    """Return True when the URL responds with an HTTP 2xx/3xx status."""
    try:
        req = urllib.request.Request(
            url, method='HEAD', headers={'User-Agent': 'cos/1.0'})
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=timeout) as resp:
            return 200 <= resp.status < 400
    except (urllib.error.URLError, urllib.error.HTTPError, OSError):
        return False


# Example:
url = 'https://example.com'
print(f'{url} is {"UP" if is_up(url) else "DOWN"}')

# With the `requests` library (nicer API):
# import requests
#
# def is_up_requests(url: str, timeout: int = 10) -> bool:
#     try:
#         resp = requests.head(url, timeout=timeout, allow_redirects=True)
#         return 200 <= resp.status_code < 400
#     except requests.RequestException:
#         return False
languages.bash:
# Print the HTTP status code (200 = up, 404/5xx = down):
curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}\n" https://example.com

# Exit 0 when up, 1 when down (useful in scripts):
if curl -sf --max-time 10 https://example.com > /dev/null; then
    echo "up"
else
    echo "down"
fi

tasks.intro: Here's how to send an email in {lang}.
tasks.notes: Never hardcode credentials — read them from environment variables. SMTP over TLS (port 587) is the standard for Gmail/Outlook; port 465 is implicit TLS. Check your provider's 'app password' requirements; plain passwords are often blocked. Always wrap the send in try/except so a bad recipient doesn't crash the script.

languages.python:
import os
import smtplib
from email.message import EmailMessage


def send_email(subject: str, body: str, to_addr: str) -> None:
    """Send plain-text email via SMTP (credentials from environment)."""
    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg['Subject'] = subject
    msg['From'] = os.environ['SMTP_USER']
    msg['To'] = to_addr
    msg.set_content(body)

    with smtplib.SMTP(os.environ['SMTP_HOST'],
                      int(os.environ.get('SMTP_PORT', '587'))) as server:
        server.starttls()
        server.login(os.environ['SMTP_USER'], os.environ['SMTP_PASS'])
        server.send_message(msg)


# Example:
# export SMTP_HOST=smtp.gmail.com SMTP_USER=you@gmail.com SMTP_PASS=app_password
